items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: Wayne Bergeron added to the mix... you go in with those kind of guys like that... Wayne Bergeron is kind of the guy now who can play anything. So he plays.

ctx.x: Did you ever write something that you couldn’t play? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

If I couldn’t play it I wouldn’t write it. But yeah, back in the day it was anything goes back then. You know Chuck Findley can play anything. You know Gary’s amazing. And Bill Reichenbach on the trombone is also just a world class player. An amazing bass trombone player, trombone player, plays drums, great writer. And Larry Williams who also was in Seawind, and Dan Higgins who has been recently, who is just a brilliant musician. So you know you go in with those kind of guys like that, and now Wayne Bergeron…

Do you get ideas in your head even when you’re not really engaged in working? I guess I think I saw your dog come through the room. And when I take my dog for a walk if I’m working on an arrangement I get these things — you know I’m thinking more about how am I going to solve this little issue. I wonder if this happens to you?

items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: I kept seeing these three names: Jerry Hey, Chuck Findley, and Gary Grant. I mean on every record that I liked... I go man who are these?

ctx.x: So you see, okay here’s Frank Wess with Basie and then you see Frank Wess over here. And here’s Snooky Young here, and then he shows up — and I used to just love watching the musical chairs. And I’m wondering if you were like that, and did you latch on to some of those lead trumpet players?

Most definitely. And more in the pop world, because I would look at all these records and I kept seeing these three names: Jerry Hey, Chuck Findley, and Gary Grant. I mean on every record that I liked, you know, whether it was an Earth, Wind and Fire record or whatever, I would just keep seeing these names. I go man who are these? They’re on everything. And everything they do sounds great too you know. And so when one of them wasn’t there, you know as a kid I’d look at those things and go, “Wow, Chuck Findley’s…
section. You’d go, “Wow, isn’t he with Count Basie? How could he be doing these two gigs at once?”
